hens_rule_text: Up to 5 poultry on RE and R-1 single-family lots, with no minimum lot size since the 2024 amendment. RR and rural zones allow 5, or up to 50 if kept 100 feet from neighboring homes.
permit_notes: The zoning text sets no permit for up to 5 poultry in RE and R-1. More birds need a Minor Conditional Use Permit in the RR zone.
setback_notes: In RE and R-1 zones the coop or shelter must be at least 10 feet from any neighboring residence and also meet accessory structure rules (Chapter 19.440). In RR and rural zones: 50 feet from neighboring homes for up to 5 birds, 100 feet for up to 50.
coop_rules: Poultry must have a coop, shelter or other permanent structure meeting accessory building standards. Premises must be kept clean and sanitary.
zoning_notes: Crowing fowl (roosters) are not permitted in RE and R-1 zones. In the RR zone up to 7 roosters are allowed on lots over 20,000 sq ft if housed overnight in a sound-reducing structure 100 feet from neighboring homes. Before March 2024, R-1 lots needed 20,000 sq ft of net area to keep any poultry.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Riverside Municipal Code Chapter 19.455 Animal Keeping (city Legistar copy, Supp. 24)
Ordinance amending Title 19, Case PR-2023-001625 (adopted March 2024)

research_notes: Read the 2024 ordinance text (case PR-2023-001625, adoption item March 2024) and the codified Chapter 19.455 from the city's Legistar. The ordinance also cites Sec. 19.445.030 in its heading, which appears to be a typo for 19.455.030. Slaughter is not addressed.
